title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a sequence, each unique item in the sequence gets its own dimension. Think about how many unique items are in a DNA sequence of $$3000$$ letters.

title: Calculating Unique Combinations
text: Consider how many unique combinations you can form with $$4$$ different letters (T, G, C, A) in a sequence of $$3000$$. What would be the total number of unique sequences?

title: Breaking Down the Problem
text: Think about the process of one-hot encoding. Each unique sequence of letters in the DNA string will have its own dimension. How does this relate to the number of possible sequences?
